task.description:
WF-03 closing gate on the ISS-0198 amendment. The diff under review is `git diff 5a8089e..HEAD` (commits df7f4ad, 83da516). DOC-UPDATER's own report is handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/step-03-amendment.json; the diagnosis it was built from is step-005-01-diagnose.json. Both are in artifacts_in. Read the DIFF, not the reports -- re-derive every verdict from the amended files themselves.

Gate the eleven acceptance criteria on step-03-amendment.json against the diff. Beyond those, five checks this gate exists for:

A. RE-RUN THE MECHANICAL CLAIMS YOURSELF. DOC-UPDATER quotes `json.loads OK; top-level keys: 18`, a corpus scan of `parseable: 585 unparseable: 0 carrying source_text: 0`, and a grep showing zero H-SIZE/6000 hits in core-directives.md and ORCHESTRATOR.md. Accepting a quoted command output is copying a claim. Run them.

B. THE NEW OPTIONAL FIELD. DOC-UPDATER declined to generalise context.requirement_text and added context.source_text instead. Judge the call on its merits, and specifically: does the amended section 2 still say unambiguously WHICH field a given piece of copied text belongs in, such that two agents would put the same text in the same field? An optional slot nobody can decide to use is worse than no slot.

C. THE 'OPTIONAL FIELD' COUNT. Section 2 previously asserted not_agent_attested was 'the one OPTIONAL field'. That sentence is now amended to name two. Verify the amended text is internally consistent with section 4.1(b)'s closed-member-set language, which was itself written this morning and is load-bearing for ISS-0191's linter.

D. AC5 CAME BACK NEGATIVE AND WAS REPORTED HONESTLY. The re-drafted corpus-maximum dispatch went 12,187 -> 7,333 chars with acceptance criteria byte-identical, and STILL flags H-SIZE-1. Check the re-draft yourself. Two questions: is the remaining 7,333 genuinely irreducible without cutting scope (the truncation failure mode H-SIZE-2 guards), and does the amended prose actually say H-SIZE-1 is advisory for this reason -- or does a reader come away thinking 6,000 is a budget? This is the criterion most likely to have been written to look like a pass.

E. SELF-CONSISTENCY. This amendment forbids restating what artifacts_in already names. Does the amendment itself obey the rule it writes, across all three touched docs?

FAIL with specific gaps named per criterion if any check fails. Do not fix anything yourself -- this is a gate. Modify no file outside handoffs/.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict re-derived from the diff itself, with the amended HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 text read directly, not from DOC-UPDATER's summary
Each of the eleven acceptance criteria on step-03-amendment.json is given an explicit PASS or FAIL with the evidence that decided it
The json.loads fence check, the corpus parseability scan, and the core-directives/ORCHESTRATOR grep are re-run first-hand and the actual outputs quoted
Check B answered: the amended section 2 is judged on whether requirement_text vs source_text is decidable by two agents reaching the same answer
Check C answered: the amended optional-field count is consistent with section 4.1(b)'s closed-member-set language
Check D answered: the re-draft is inspected first-hand, and the amended prose is judged on whether it reads as advisory or as a budget
Check E answered: the amendment is checked against its own rule across all three touched docs
Any FAIL names the specific gap and the file/section, never a general impression
No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step
